- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤-0.3) and prices are falling, model often underestimates drop; increase forecast downward by 3–8% to match true decline.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged overshoot; cap forecast at 1–2 days above true peak.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.3–0.7), model often fails to capture mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 3–5-day moving average of recent history.  
- If model forecast is consistently higher than true outcome over 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day for next 7–14 days, especially if sentiment is weak or negative.  
- If true outcome shows early sharp decline after a peak, model often lags; adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag in true drop, especially if sentiment is bearish.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is volatile or inconsistent, reduce forecast variance by 15–30% to avoid overconfidence in short-term momentum.
